Maya: quick profiler dump from last night's multi-gpu run — we've been hitting sporadic OOMs during streaming long chats. snapshot below (nvprof summary pasted).

```
nvprof mem summary (canary run 3):
GPU0 total 48.0GiB
- model shards (TP)    30.8GiB
- kv_cache             9.2GiB
- temp/per-op          3.6GiB
- intergpu comm bufs   2.4GiB
- free                 1.0GiB
Observed transient +2.5GiB when attention kernel switched workspace. OOMs cluster around token boundary spikes.
```

Omar: huh, attention kernel change? when did that land?

Jin: rolled kernel-v2 on canary last week. it auto-selects FFT-style attention when seq_len >= 1024. that ups workspace per-replica from ~200MB -> ~1.2GB in our builds.

Priya: ugh so per-TP-shard that becomes huge. KV cache mostly constant; the problem is temp allocations + kernel workspace + comm overhead sum to > available during bursts. can we pool the per-op workspace?

Omar: we already have a comm buffer pool but it's scoped per-stream+shard; fragmentation + different lifetimes stop reuse. proposal: global per-device temp pool with a small reserved "watermark" for kernel workspace, and a runtime knob to pick memory-preferred kernel when free < 2GiB.

Maya: quick experiment: set REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL_PREF=memory on canary and re-ran the same prompt set. workspace dropped from ~1.2GiB -> ~0.25GiB per replica, OOMs disappeared. perf tradeoff: throughput -6%, p50 latency +40ms. NVprof snippet:

```
Before: ws=1.2GiB, peak transient=+2.5GiB, OOMs x8
After:  ws=0.25GiB, peak transient=+0.4GiB, OOMs 0
```

Command to toggle:
```
export REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL_PREF=memory
# or: REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL_PREF=latency
```

Jin: nice find. 6% throughput hit might be acceptable for our SLA tiers (dedicated vs hosted). alternative is to avoid switching to the big-workspace kernel for borderline seq lengths — limit to seq>=2048 or add upfront workspace reserve accounting.

Priya: another vector: NCCL ephemeral buffers. our traces show NCCL alloc spikes aligned with TP syncs at token boundaries. looks like small collective calls are allocating temporary staging buffers frequently. reusing a durable comm pool across collectives could reduce the transient memory pressure.

Omar: agree. plan to prototype three changes: (a) per-op workspace cap knob (enforceable at runtime), (b) global temp-pool with LRU eviction and fast alloc/free, (c) make NCCL staging bufs durable per-device instead of per-call. I'll put this in the rm-memory branch.

Maya: Jin, can you validate kernel fallback policy (ensure we don't flip to fast kernel mid-request)? Priya, can you run perf/regression eval on the prompt set (long-chats + short bursts) to quantify latency/cost tradeoffs? Omar to prototype pools + cap.

Omar: quick implementation note: prototype uses a fixed-size cudaMalloc-driven arena with a lock-free freelist per-stream; when arena exhausted we fall back to cudaMalloc (to avoid hard OOM) and emit metric redwood.runtime.temp_pool.evictions.

Priya: also testing batching heuristic change: combine microbatches at token-boundaries so collectives are fewer but slightly larger — smoothing reduced NCCL spikes on a local run. need cluster run to confirm.

infra-bot: scheduled smoke test for rm-memory branch on canary cluster — Tue 16:00 UTC. cc: @Maya @Omar @Jin @Priya :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks. keeping this thread for status updates. :spiral_note_pad:
